description: Germanium is a chemical element with symbol Ge and atomic number 32. It is a lustrous, hard-brittle, grayish-white metalloid in the carbon group that is chemically similar to silicon. Like silicon, germanium naturally reacts and forms complexes with oxygen in nature.
uses: Elemental germanium is used as a semiconductor in transistors and various electronic devices, with major end uses including fibre-optic systems, infrared optics, solar cell applications, and light-emitting diodes (LEDs). Germanium compounds are also used for polymerization catalysts and in the production of nanowires, while organogermanium compounds are useful in organometallic chemistry.
characteristics: Under standard conditions, germanium is a brittle, silvery-white semiconductor with a metallic luster and diamond cubic crystal structure. It is one of the few substances that expands as it solidifies from the molten state, and has been produced in highly pure crystalline form with impurity of only one part in 10^10. Elemental germanium starts to oxidize slowly in air at around 250 °C, forming germanium dioxide, and occurs mostly in the oxidation state +4 although many +2 compounds are known.
